id="ADR-0001" title="Use JWT for v1 agent capability tokens; defer SPIFFE to v2" status="Proposed" inferred=false
author="Donald Gifford" created="2026-05-10"
summary=""
context="The Agent Capability Tokens RFC (sibling, RFC-NNNN) specifies a signed-token model for too…"
decision="Use **Vault-Transit-signed JWT** as the v1 capability token format. Defer SPIFFE/SPIRE mig…"
consequences positive=5 negative=4 neutral=2
alternatives=0 open-questions=0 references=7

positive line=93
  text="**No new operational footprint.** Vault is already in the stack (existing Vault JIT pattern). Using Vault Transit for signing adds one secrets-engine mount; no new servers, no new agents."

positive line=96
  text="**Familiar trust model.** JWTs are well-understood across the team; the verification story is \"fetch public key, validate signature\" — straightforward."

positive line=99
  text="**Direct Vault JWT-auth integration.** Vault's existing `jwt`/`oidc` auth method consumes our tokens natively for STS issuance, no glue code."

positive line=101
  text="**Lower learning curve.** No SPIFFE concepts (trust domains, federation, SVIDs, registration entries) to onboard new team members to."

positive line=103
  text="**Faster v1.** Phase 2 of the capability RFC (controller as token issuer) is days of work with JWT; would be weeks with SPIFFE bootstrapping."

negative line=110
  text="**No native federation.** Cross-cluster or external-workload identity will require a migration. The RFC documents that migration target as v2 work."

negative line=112
  text="**No native attenuation.** If we want delegated capability tokens later (agent A → agent B with subset scopes), we'd need either controller-mediated re-issuance (works fine, less elegant) or a migration to Macaroons / Biscuit (heavier change). For v1's single-agent-per-run model, this doesn't bite."

negative line=116
  text="**Revocation is partial.** Vault Transit doesn't natively revoke JWTs. The RFC handles this with a small Redis-backed `jti` revocation set with TTL ≤ max token lifetime. SPIFFE has the same limitation; not a meaningful differentiator."

negative line=120
  text="**Public-key cache is a soft consistency point.** Verifiers cache the Vault Transit public key with a 5-minute TTL. During key rotation, there is a window where a verifier might still trust the old key. SPIFFE has analogous trust-bundle caching."

neutral line=129
  text="**Both options end up with claim-bearing tokens.** The capability RFC's claim structure works in either JWT or JWT-SVID form. The migration cost is mostly issuer / verifier infrastructure, not the claim schema."

neutral line=132
  text="**Performance is comparable.** Both verify in microseconds. The difference is operational complexity, not runtime cost."

reference line=166 url=""
  text="Sibling: RFC-NNNN Agent Capability Tokens — specifies the full capability model this ADR implements the token format for"

reference line=168 url=""
  text="Sibling: ADR-NNNN Use OPA for scope policy evaluation — the policy engine the verified claims feed into"

reference line=170 url=""
  text="Internal: Agent platform RFC + DESIGN suite — existing Vault integration this builds on"
